chunks: And from a letter of his (peace be upon him) which he wrote to Shurayh ibn al-Harith, his judge.

key_terms.شُرَيْحُ: Shurayh, a proper name of the judge
key_terms.قَاضِيهِ: his judge, indicating the official capacity of the recipient

ai.seo_question: Who was the recipient of Imam Ali's letter in Nahj al-Balagha Chapter 1?
ai.summary: This heading introduces a seminal epistle from Imam Ali (peace be upon him) to Shurayh ibn al-Harith, his chief judge in Kufa, marking the beginning of a detailed discourse on judicial ethics and administrative justice. It sets the stage for the Imam’s comprehensive instructions on how to administer law with fairness, integrity, and fear of God, reflecting the practical application of governance during the early Caliphate. The letter is often cited in Shia jurisprudence as a primary source for understanding the qualities of a qadi (judge) and the principles of equitable judgment.
